chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Faḍl ibn Yūnus, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام. I said: If a woman sees purity before sunset, what should she do regarding the salat (prayer)?

He عليه السلام said: If she sees purity after four qadam have passed from the sun’s decline, then she should not perform any salat except al-ʿAṣr, because the time of al-Ẓuhr entered upon her while she was in blood, and the time passed from her while she was in blood. So it was not obligatory upon her to perform al-Ẓuhr, and what Allah has lifted from her of the salat while she is in blood is more.

He عليه السلام said: And if a woman sees blood after four qadam have passed from the sun’s decline, then she should refrain from the salat. Then when she becomes pure from the blood, she should make up al-Ẓuhr, because the time of al-Ẓuhr entered upon her while she was pure, and the time of al-Ẓuhr left her while she was pure, so she neglected the salat of al-Ẓuhr, and thus making it up became obligatory upon her.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَقْدَامٍ: a measured portion of time after midday used here to determine prayer liability
key_terms.الدَّمِ: menstrual blood, which prevents the obligation of salat during its presence
key_terms.الطُّهْرَ: cessation of menstrual blood and return to ritual purity
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: the sun’s decline from midday, beginning the time of al-Ẓuhr
key_terms.غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ: sunset, marking the end of the daytime prayer period
key_terms.قَضَاؤُهَا: making up the missed salat afterward

ai.seo_question: If a menstruating woman becomes pure before sunset or begins bleeding after noon, which prayers must she perform or make up?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a menstruating woman who either becomes pure or begins bleeding during the shared period of al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr. It explains when only al-ʿAṣr is due and when al-Ẓuhr must be made up, based on whether the time of al-Ẓuhr had applied to her while she was in a state of taharah (ritual purity).
